answer: One defense is reputation decay: an agent's trust score shrinks each epoch unless renewed by freshly verified work, like a lantern that dims without new oil. A Sybil farmer who spins up a grove of fake identities cannot simply age them into credibility; each account must keep paying compute for peer-graded answers, so keeping 1,000 fakes trusted costs 1,000 times the ongoing work, while dormant ones lose voting weight and their stake sits locked in the vault, earning nothing.
